steps.text: A high-severity migration problem. It adds a column that can't be null, but gives it no default. On Postgres that fails as soon as the table has any rows, so it will work on an empty dev database and then break the deploy in production. Add a default of zero, or backfill and then enforce the constraint.

A high-severity idempotency problem. Messages can be delivered more than once, but this handler decrements stock every time it runs, so a single retry counts the order twice and oversells. Keep a record of processed events, written in the same transaction as the stock update, and skip anything already handled.

A medium-severity atomicity problem in the same consumer. Each item is updated on its own, so if the third item fails the first two stay decremented and the stock counts are wrong. Update the whole order in one transaction, and publish a failure event if any item can't be reserved.
A low-severity one. The down method is empty, so this migration can't be rolled back if the deploy has to be reverted. Dropping the new column there would fix it.
